admission.justification: Reporting would-create for an existing journal-owned ref misstates the actual recovery plan and confuses contract absence with source absence; the two-stage same-journal operation pins their independent facts.

applicability: External-memory source-branch facts in first-leaf worktree-start preview carrying the owner-admitted unpublished atomic parent, including partial-bootstrap journal recovery.
conditions: The exact configured/task-derived memory repository, branch and pinned readable base were already validated by parent admission.
Would-create requires both explicit dry run/unpublished non-symlink parent and actual absence of the exact named memory ref.
If the journal-owned exact ref exists before parent publication, the original named-ref owner returns existing.
Actual apply/default use still requires its exact source ref and keeps the original bootstrap/recovery authority.
exclusions: Creation or advancement of protected refs, which belongs to the existing actual bootstrap/landing owners.
Invented alternate source branches, replacement journals or manually materialized parent contracts.
Code-side source-state reporting, which has its own owner.

evidence: notes/reports/260928-MIK-L47-review-R2.md; reviewer F1-public.txt 1 passed in 18.69s, four equal inventories and actual same-journal apply; F1-registered-proof.tar.gz with raw receipts and product bytes.

statement: The repaired memory preview uses would-create only when the exact admitted unpublished parent memory ref is absent and reports existing for the journal-owned ref already created.
